name: RUINWALK: Shelf Archaeology AR Challenge
description: One of the earliest successful AR urban exploration titles specific to GLMZ, RUINWALK tasks players with physically navigating pre-Collapse infrastructure in Tier 1 Shelf districts — finding and documenting hidden architectural remnants, mapping abandoned transit tunnels, and cataloguing what the game calls 'ghost structures' overlaid in AR on standing ruins. Built by a single Tier 2 developer named Osamu Ferreira-Okafor, it was distributed free for two years before a Tier 3 heritage organization purchased the IP. The game inadvertently became the most comprehensive documentation of Shelf infrastructure ever compiled, because players did the fieldwork.
story_hooks: A RUINWALK ghost-structure overlay in a specific Shelf block keeps showing a building that never existed — but three players who've seen it independently describe the same interior layout.
The original developer, Osamu Ferreira-Okafor, who sold the IP under financial duress, has been quietly building a new version of the game with functionality the buyer doesn't know about.
A player's RUINWALK documentation of an 'abandoned' tunnel is the only evidence that a current corponation construction project is about to destroy a protected pre-Collapse cultural site.
